findings.title: STD-1's own 'fixed' evidence command still does not reproduce the number it cites — same failure class as the original finding, now inside the fix
findings.evidence: wave1-ci-gates-1026-1027.md line 196-197, written during this fix round to answer STD-1, now reads: 'The command that reproduces that number exactly is `grep -c '\''world-gate\.mjs" tests/'\'' .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml` = 24'. Ran it verbatim on the worktree at 2eb14b58d: it returns 23, not 24. The reason is line 586, the one `--test` invocation: `node "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:?...}/scripts/ci/world-gate.mjs" --test tests/body-census-guard-db.test.mjs` — the literal substring `world-gate.mjs" tests/` never occurs there because `--test ` sits between the closing quote and `tests/`, so this one line silently drops out of the count. Independently re-verified the SUBSTANTIVE claim two other ways and it holds: a Python `yaml.safe_load` parse of the real YAML structure (not text-matching) counts exactly 24 `node .../world-gate.mjs ...tests/*.mjs` invocations across the 7 steps and 0 bare ones; `node scripts/ci/world-gate.selftest.mjs`'s own wiring-guard cell (which uses a permissive regex, `/(^|\s)node\s/` plus `/\btests\/\S+\.mjs/`, exactly built to survive a `--test` flag) also finds 24 and 0 unwired. So AC1's real number (24, all wired) is correct and independently confirmed; only the report's restated verification command for it is wrong, in the same way the original STD-1 finding was — an evidence command that does not literally reproduce its own cited figure.
findings.required_fix: Restate the report's command to one that actually returns 24, e.g. `grep -cE 'node "\$\{GITHUB_WORKSPACE.*world-gate\.mjs"' .github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml` (verified = 24 on this worktree), or point at the selftest's own wiring-guard cell as the reproducible check instead of a hand-written grep. Not required for merge — the underlying AC1 claim is true and independently verified by two other methods.

findings.title: The rewritten discriminator's absolute phrasing ('blocked=0 refusals=0 = belt regression') has one unstated theoretical exception, subsumed by the newly-filed third-race ticket
findings.evidence: intake-batch-e2e.mjs:136-140 and README.md:1440-1443 state unconditionally: 'blocked = 0 AND refusals = 0 — the belt is not counting firm P's refusals at all. That is a REGRESSION.' Traced through the code: `pWatch.blocked`/`refusals` only ever go non-zero once at least one belt sweep has run and seen a still-live child to refuse. If the World terminalises BOTH of firm P's children before the very first sweep of the P-loop (not merely before the leg's end, which is the race #1028 already documents), the loop would time out at 5 s with `refusals=0 blocked=0` — the identical census the rule attributes solely to a belt regression — even though no belt defect occurred. This is a narrower, strictly-less-likely sub-case of the same race already filed as #1028 (measured child death time ~8 s vs. a first sweep that in every recorded run lands in single-digit to low-hundred-digit milliseconds after `applyPoison()`), so it is not a new failure mode, and both reviewers already agreed the general race should not block this change. It is simply not called out as a caveat on the rule's own wording.
findings.required_fix: None required for merge. Optional: when #1028 is worked, extend the rule's stated caveat (or the fixture) to cover 'children already terminal before the loop's first sweep' as the same race, not only 'children terminal by the leg's end'.

summary: Re-checked the fix round (3d57866da for #1027, 2eb14b58d for #1026) against both code-review axes' 13 findings plus SPEC-META-01's two interim residuals, by reading the full diff dd3d335dd...2eb14b58d, the whole LEG 4 block, world-gate.mjs/selftest.mjs, and the action.yml diff, and by re-running every cheap check named. RESULT: every finding above note severity from both reports is fixed, and SPEC-META-01's two 'introduced during review' problems (the vacuous firm-Q control asserting a constant; the un-polled single-shot door read) are both closed in the committed code — the firm-Q control is dropped with a sound argument (`cancel_blocked` is gated on `state='cancelling'` in migration 0229:1088, independent of the belt's own correctness, so a healthy firm's control could only ever assert a fixed value), and the door verdict (`pWatch.doorVerdict`) is captured INSIDE the same bounded `pollToDeadline` loop that counts the refusal and the blocked flag, not read again afterward. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: (1) two independent deadlines, `LEG4_P_DEADLINE_MS=5000` and `LEG4_Q_DEADLINE_MS=8000`, each justified in the file from the report's own measurements (1516 ms / 2774 ms worst cases), replacing the single 30 s constant; the P-loop's break condition is `refusals>=1 && blocked>=1 && doorVerdict==='canceller_not_active'`, all three read on the same sweep; a deadline throw always calls `leg4Diagnosis`, which carries both firms, both parents, both states, every child's Work status, cumulative refusals/blocked, and a freshly-read `cancel_blocked` for both firms. Traced both requested scenarios: a belt that records a CLR04 refusal as a success keeps `refusals`/`blocked` at 0 forever, so the P-loop times out at 5 s with a message reading 'no sweep reported a refusal, a blocked parent and the door's own canceller_not_active together' and a `refusals=0 blocked=0` census — this is exactly what the implementer's own vacuity-control run (clara_814, RED at 11 sweeps/5560 ms) shows and I did not need to re-run it. A World that terminalises firm P's children first (the disclosed, out-of-scope third race) is caught later, at the unpolled disjointness assert, and its message shows the historical `blocked>=1`/`cancel_blocked=canceller_not_active` captured earlier in the run alongside the now-terminal state — a reader can tell the two reds apart from the message text and the counters alone, as designed. (2) No remaining assertion in LEG 4 is an uncatchable tautology of the kind #1027 exists to remove; the few post-loop `assert.ok`/`assert.equal` calls restate a condition the preceding poll already guaranteed (documentation-as-code, present before this fix round too and not itself a defect), and the one true vacuous control (firm Q's) is gone. (3) Built a scratch copy of world-gate.mjs/selftest.mjs/action.yml OUTSIDE the worktree and confirmed by actually running it: appending an unwired `node tests/sneaky-new-leg.mjs` line makes `world-gate.selftest.mjs` fail (exit 1) naming the exact line; emptying the action to 0 invocations fails the '20+ legs' floor by name rather than passing vacuously; the peak-memory sampler cannot fail a leg (wrapped in try/catch, exit code comes only from the child's own code/signal), costs nothing off Linux (`enabled` gate skips arming the timer and every sample call entirely), and its line is greppable (`[world-gate] peak ...`), all confirmed by the selftest's dedicated cells and by code inspection. (4) README's #1026 section now compares like for like — '2048 without the bound ran 0:56 and 1:14; 2048 with it ran 2:00 to 3:22' — and states plainly 'THE BOUND, NOT THE BUDGET, IS WHAT BUYS THE 25% MARGIN', with the third-race wall-clock question explicitly marked unverified rather than silently dropped. (5) Both commits (3d57866da, 2eb14b58d) name their ticket in the subject, bundle README + code + test changes together (no docs left for a later commit), and end with a Co-Authored-By line; the disclosed follow-up 'third race' ticket has actually been filed as #1028 (`gh issue view 1028`), matching the ticket body drafted in the implementer's report. RE-RUN MYSELF, all green: `node scripts/ci/world-gate.selftest.mjs` (19/19, wiring guard and inverse cell both PASS); `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` exit 0 with 'world-gate selftest: OK' in the chain; `pnpm typecheck` clean (apps/web, packages/runtime); `node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs` OK (312 files); a real YAML parse (Python `yaml.safe_load`, not text-matching) of action.yml: 7 steps, 24 launcher-wrapped `tests/*.mjs` invocations, 0 bare, matching both review reports' counts exactly. Did NOT run any World leg. Two residuals found, both at or below minor and neither introduced a regression in substance: RECHECK-STD1-01 (minor) — the fix round's own restated 'reproduces 24 exactly' command for STD-1 actually returns 23 on this worktree because of the one `--test` invocation line, the same evidence-precision defect STD-1 originally flagged, now recurring in the fix itself; the underlying AC1 claim (24 wired, 0 bare) is independently true by two other methods. RECHECK-1027-NOTE-01 (note) — the rewritten discriminator's 'blocked=0 refusals=0 always means a belt regression' rule has one theoretical gap (children terminal before the very first sweep, not just by the leg's end), which is a narrower sub-case of the already-filed #1028 and not a new defect. Nothing above minor remains, so this recheck accepts.
